verses.zh: 我爱耶和华，因为他听了我的声音和我的恳求。
verses.en: I love the Lordbecause he heard my plea for mercy[NOTE:1]
notes: Psalm 116. The psalmist thanks the Lord for delivering him from a life threatening crisis and promises to tell the entire covenant community what God has done for him.

verses.zh: 他既向我侧耳，我一生要求告他。
verses.en: and listened to me.[NOTE:1] As long as I live, I will call to him when I need help.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “I love because the Lord heard my voice, my pleas.” It is possible that “the Lord” originally appeared directly after “I love” and was later accidentally misplaced. The translation assumes the prefixed verbal form is a preterite. The psalmist recalls that God heard his cry for help (note the perfect in v. 2a and the narrative in vv. 3-4).
Heb “because he turned his ear to me.”

verses.zh: 死亡的绳索缠绕我；阴间的痛苦抓住我；我遭遇患难愁苦。
verses.en: The ropes of death tightened around me,[NOTE:1] the snares[NOTE:2] of Sheol confronted me.I was confronted[NOTE:3] with trouble and sorrow.
notes: Heb “and in my days I will cry out.”
Heb “surrounded me.”

The Hebrew noun מֵצַר (metsar, “straits; distress”) occurs only here, Ps 118:5 and Lam 1:3. If retained, it refers to Sheol as a place where one is confined or severely restricted (cf. BDB 865 s.v. מֵצַר, “the straits of Sheol”; NIV “the anguish of the grave”; NRSV “the pangs of Sheol”). However, HALOT 624 s.v. מֵצַר suggests an emendation to מְצָדֵי (metsade, “snares of”), a rare noun attested in Job 19:6 and Eccl 7:26. This proposal, which is reflected in the translation, produces better parallelism with “ropes” in the preceding line.

verses.zh: 那时，我便求告耶和华的名，说：耶和华啊，求你救我的灵魂！
verses.en: I called on the name of the Lord,“Please, Lord, rescue my life!”

verses.zh: 耶和华有恩惠，有公义；我们的　神以怜悯为怀。
verses.en: The Lord is merciful and fair;our God is compassionate.

verses.zh: 耶和华保护愚人；我落到卑微的地步，他救了我。
verses.en: The Lord protects[NOTE:1] the untrained;[NOTE:2] I was in serious trouble[NOTE:3] and he delivered me.
notes: The translation assumes the prefixed verbal form is a preterite. The psalmist recalls the crisis from which the Lord delivered him.
Heb “guards.” The active participle indicates this is a characteristic of the Lord.
Or “the [morally] naive,” that is, the one who is young and still in the process of learning right from wrong and distinguishing wisdom from folly. See Ps 19:7.

verses.zh: 我的心哪！你要仍归安乐，因为耶和华用厚恩待你。
verses.en: Rest once more, my soul,[NOTE:1] for the Lord has vindicated you.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “I was low.”
Heb “return, my soul, to your place of rest.”

verses.zh: 主啊，你救我的命免了死亡，救我的眼免了流泪，救我的脚免了跌倒。
verses.en: Yes,[NOTE:1] Lord,[NOTE:2] you rescued my life from death,kept my eyes from tears and my feet from stumbling.
notes: The Hebrew idiom גָּמַל עַל (gamal ʿal) means “to repay,” here in a positive sense (cf. Ps 13:5).
Or “for.”

verses.zh: 我要在耶和华面前行活人之路。
verses.en: I will serve[NOTE:1] the Lordin the land[NOTE:2] of the living.
notes: “Lord” is supplied here in the translation for clarification.
Heb “walk before” (see Ps 56:13). On the meaning of the Hebrew idiom, see the notes at 2 Kgs 20:3/Isa 38:3.

verses.zh: 我因信，所以如此说话；我受了极大的困苦。
verses.en: I had faith when I said,“I am severely oppressed.”

verses.zh: 我曾急促地说：人都是说谎的！
verses.en: I rashly declared,[NOTE:1] “All men are liars.”
notes: Heb “lands, regions.”

verses.zh: 我拿甚么报答耶和华向我所赐的一切厚恩？
verses.en: How can I repay the Lordfor all his acts of kindness to me?

verses.zh: 我要举起救恩的杯，称扬耶和华的名。
verses.en: I will celebrate my deliverance[NOTE:1] and call on the name of the Lord.
notes: Heb “I said in my haste.”

verses.zh: 我要在他众民面前向耶和华还我的愿。
verses.en: I will fulfill my vows to the Lordbefore all his people.

verses.zh: 在耶和华眼中，看圣民之死极为宝贵。
verses.en: The Lord valuesthe lives of his faithful followers.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “a cup of deliverance I will lift up.” Perhaps this alludes to a drink offering the psalmist will present as he thanks the Lord for his deliverance. See v. 17.

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，我真是你的仆人；我是你的仆人，是你婢女的儿子。你已经解开我的绑索。
verses.en: Yes, Lord! I am indeed your servant;I am your servant, the son of your female servant.[NOTE:1] You saved me from death.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “precious in the eyes of the Lord [is] the death of his godly ones.” The point is not that God delights in or finds satisfaction in the death of his followers! The psalmist, who has been delivered from death, affirms that the life-threatening experiences of God’s followers get God’s attention, just as a precious or rare object would attract someone’s eye. See Ps 72:14 for a similar expression of this belief.

Heb “I am your servant, the son of your female servant.” The phrase “son of a female servant” (see also Ps 86:16) is used of a son born to a secondary wife or concubine (Exod 23:12). In some cases the child’s father is the master of the house (see Gen 21:10, 13; Judg 9:18). It may used metaphorically and idiomatically to emphasize the psalmist’s humility before the Lord and his status as the Lord’s servant. Or it may be a reference to the psalmist’s own mother who also was a servant of the Lord.

verses.zh: 我要以感谢为祭献给你，又要求告耶和华的名。
verses.en: I will present a thank offering to you,and call on the name of the Lord.

verses.zh: 我要在他众民面前，在耶和华殿的院内，在耶路撒冷当中，向耶和华还我的愿。你们要赞美耶和华！
verses.en: I will fulfill my vows to the Lordbefore all his people,
in the courts of the Lord’s temple,in your midst, O Jerusalem.Praise the Lord!
